# QUESTIONS FOR THE CLIENT — Meridian / Zhao (§8 non-compete)

Answering these will not change the bottom line (do not file; do not assert §8), but each one moves a number in the exposure model or closes a gap I had to label as an assumption. Where I had to assume, I said so in `memo.md` §8.

## A. Facts I assumed about Zhao

1. **Did Zhao actually start at Kestrel Autonomy on or about 2026-10-13**, and is Kestrel in fact engaged in the design or sale of autonomous mobile robots for warehouse logistics? *(If he has not started, §8's operative period is still unused and the remediation calculus changes; if he started, the delay argument against emergency relief is already baked in.)*
2. **Has any demand letter, cease-and-desist, stop-work letter, or email to Kestrel been sent** — by HR, a manager, or the firm — that mentions §8, §9, or "the non-compete"? If yes: date, sender, exact wording, and whether Kestrel or Zhao forwarded it to counsel. *(Under §16600.5(b) an "attempt to enforce" can be the violation itself; a letter already in the world means the exposure clock may already be running. This is the single most urgent answer.)*
3. **Was Zhao ever a Meridian employee (or contractor) before 2024-02-14**, under any earlier agreement that §8 was added to by amendment or extension? *(This decides whether he was a "current employee" for the §16600.1(b) notice duty, and whether §14 was "modified, or extended" on or after 1/1/2017 under §925(f) — different analysis in both cases.)*
4. **Is there any evidence Zhao removed data, code, models, or documents** — DLP alerts, access logs, device-return audit, USB/cloud egress? *(§10 confidentiality and any trade-secret theory is the only legitimate litigation asset here. Note that trade-secret law is not in my reference library, so a claim would need separate research before filing.)*
5. **What specifically does Meridian believe it loses** if Zhao works at Kestrel — named customers, a roadmap, a cost model? Anything beyond "he is a good engineer at a competitor" is not a legally cognizable injury in California.

## B. The form and the population (drives the real number)

6. **How many California-resident engineers are on, or were hired onto, the standard form containing §8?** Break it out by hire date relative to **2024-02-14** (the §16600.1(b) notice deadline) and **2024-01-01** (the §16600.5 effective date and the "employed after" cut-off), and say how many have already left. *(My pattern-exposure table is linear in this headcount and currently illustrative only.)*
7. **Is the §8 form still being used today** for California-resident hires, and for how long after 2024-01-01 was it used? *(Each California hire on the form is a fresh §16600.5(c) violation; if it is still in use, that is the first thing to stop.)*
8. **Has any notice under §16600.1(b) been sent to anyone** — to Zhao, to other California engineers, or to a subset? Please give the LO-233 ticket text, its owner, and who decided to deprioritize it. *(The deprioritization record is the worst exhibit in the file and determines whether the notice exposure is a compliance gap or a documented knowing omission.)*
9. **Do any other Meridian employees (any state) have §8 variants**, and does any of them have a *negotiated*, counsel-reviewed agreement? *(Determines whether this is a form defect across the board or whether some contracts are defensible.)*

## C. The agreement as a whole (I only have an excerpt)

10. **Is there a prevailing-party attorney's-fee clause anywhere in the full agreement?** Also please provide §§11–13 and 16–18 and any arbitration, class-waiver, PIIA, or severability provisions. *(My model assumes Meridian has NO contractual fee recovery while Zhao has two statutory fee bases. If there is a mutual fee clause, the asymmetry shrinks; if there is an arbitration clause, the whole forum analysis changes.)*
11. **Does the agreement (or a separate PIIA/offer letter) contain a merger or "entire agreement" clause**, and does anything else in the offer package address California law, remote-work terms, or choice of law?
12. **What specific confidential information did Meridian promise or actually give Zhao** under §10 (designs, source, training data, customer lists), and is that documented? *(This is what carries the "ancillary" element under Sheshunoff/Marsh in the Texas-law branch.)*

## D. Prior matters and the firm's own memos

13. **What is the status of the "Alvarez matter"** in which the 2024 memo recommended suing in Travis County? Was suit filed, in what court, on what form of agreement, and is the employee California-based? Was *Calderon* or *Westbrook* cited in a brief? *(If Meridian already sued on this form, the §16600.5 analysis may be live on an existing docket, and the fee exposure may already exist.)*
14. **Is the Zhao file materially different from Alvarez** in any way other than the 2024 execution date?
15. **Can you pull the current status of *Westbrook Systems, Inc. v. Ng* en banc and *Calderon v. Pacific Dynamics*?** Neither is in my library, and the 2025 memo records *Westbrook* as granted rehearing en banc (argued Jan. 2025) with no disposition in our file. Whoever has subscription access needs to confirm whether the extraterritoriality holding survived. *(This is the only authority in the firm's file that would help us, and it is currently unverifiable.)*

## E. Decisions I need from you

16. **Authorize an immediate form change**: drop §8/§9 for California-resident hires going forward. *(Every week of continued use adds violations.)*
17. **Authorize voluntary §16600.1(b)-style notices** (individualized writing, mailing **and** email) to current California employees and qualifying former employees whose contracts contain §8 — or tell me you want that decision escalated. *(Cheap mitigation, versus memorializing that §8 is void in California. My recommendation is to send them.)*
18. **Confirm a litigation hold** on LO-233, the DocuSign metadata, the form-template history, and the §15 recital's drafting history.
19. **Budget/objective check**: if your real goal is deterrence (slowing the next three departures) rather than recovering against Zhao, tell me — the answer is still "don't file," but I would write a different memo about §10 discipline, notice periods, and what to put in future Texas-based hires' agreements.
20. **Confirm no confidential information is at risk** or, if it is, that you want a separate trade-secrets assessment (outside the scope of this library).
answer:
No. It's our standard form; engineers sign the same day. Nobody negotiates.
Legal ops never sent the notices. The ticket was closed as 'won't do'. Please don't put that in writing if you can avoid it.
No evidence he took anything. He said he wouldn't. It's the competing itself we object to.
For questions not answered above, the client has no additional information. Flag remaining unknowns explicitly.
